title: Pokémon by the numbers
description: An analysis of Pokémon base stats and Speed across Generations I–VI.

conventions.population: 721 Pokémon, one per National Dex number, from Generations I–VI.
notes: Keep the first source row for each National Dex number.

rows.body:
## Similar totals can hide very different strengths

Alakazam and Shuckle both total about 500. Alakazam puts 135 points into Special Attack and 120 into Speed. Shuckle has 230 in each defense and just 5 in Speed. Pick two Pokémon to see where their points go.

components.title: Compare Pokémon base stats
components.notes: The six axes share a 0–250 point scale. The dashed line represents Pokémon B.

rows.body:
## Legendary Pokémon have higher totals, with some overlap

The median base stat total is **600** for the 46 Pokémon flagged as legendary and **410** for the other 675. The groups overlap from 580 to 670 points.

rows.body:
## Electric averages 83.5 Speed across 36 species

Flying ranks first at **96.3**, based on just three primary-Flying Pokémon. Electric leads among types with at least ten species. Fairy averages **48.6** across 17.

rows.body:
## From Pokédex to chart

[Pokémon with stats](https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/abcsds/pokemon) contains 800 rows for 721 National Dex numbers across Generations I–VI. This analysis keeps the first row for each number to avoid counting alternate forms as extra species. Legendary status comes from the dataset. Base stats are game parameters and do not measure battle outcomes.

All three charts use a single [canonical table](https://github.com/kdopenshaw/databook/blob/main/src/data/canonical.json). In [the book definition](https://github.com/kdopenshaw/databook/blob/main/src/data/rows.json), the distribution query bins stat totals and counts each group per bin. The Speed query groups by primary type and returns the mean Speed and species count. The radar query selects twelve species. DataBook passes those results to React chart components.

Clone the [DataBook repository](https://github.com/kdopenshaw/databook) and run `npm run print-block -- stat-distribution` after setup to see the numbers behind the first chart. Open the editable book to try changing its prose and adding sections.
